column3: propagation is the observed boundary (TransactionBoundary.observed, TransactionRecorder.java:271): NESTED for a SQLAlchemy SAVEPOINT, REQUIRES_NEW only for a second live, non-AUTOCOMMIT transaction on a different DBAPI connection begun by the same task or thread, NEW with no other live transaction, UNKNOWN otherwise; deviations: a shared DBAPI connection (StaticPool), a parent inherited by a child task or executor thread and a begin whose own connection is AUTOCOMMIT beside a live transaction are UNKNOWN because SQLAlchemy shows no ownership there (BootUI reads Spring's transaction manager), and an enclosing transaction is a parent only when this recorder recorded it

A begin that fails is detected from SQLAlchemy's handle_error (the connection is set, in_transaction() is False and the connection holds an open row) instead of Spring's failed begin callback (TransactionRecorder.beginFailedTransaction): the row is UNKNOWN with begun false, no SQL statements and no connections, its message goes through the masker, and a failing commit or rollback is not a failed begin; a failed SAVEPOINT statement drops its savepoint row the same way
sharpit's activity feed is built from the panel buffers and keeps no failed-begin filter wording (JournalActivityFeed.java:660,907); the failed-begin row is in the transactions report
sharpit's request profile has no transaction slot, so there is no failed-begin wording to port (RequestJournalProfiles.java:627)
A connection that cannot be opened raises before SQLAlchemy emits a begin event, so no transaction row exists to mark; BootUI records the failed begin only when the transaction manager started one
